newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's BPI '96 cons net rises 56 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's BPI '96 cons net rises 56 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Cash flow before minority interests 31.9 vs 15.8

NOTE: Banco Portugues de Investimento said its 1996 results were not directly comparable with those of 1995 because of the acquisition of state controlled bank Banco de Fomento e Exterior (BFE) in August 1996. "The consolidation of BFE took place from October 1, 1996, and so the results include BFE's accounts for the last quarter of 1996," BPI said in a statement.
BPI said "goodwill" of 47 billion escudos from the acquisition of BFE was amortised in its 1996 accounts by a transfer from reserves and that it would have no impact on future results.

BPI said it raised its provisions sharply, well above the requirements of the Bank of Portugal, to 17.5 billion escudos, including a seven billion escudo adjustment due to the purchase of BFE. The bank gave no figures for provisions for 1995. The board decided to propose to the general assembly on March 21 a gross dividend of 85 escudos per share, which represents a five percent increase over the 100 escudos paid in 1995, adjusted for a capital increase at end-1995.
